title: The heap by hand: new and delete

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Build the waiting shelf here and run it, and watch which repairs end and when.

tasks.title: Take in a repair that has to wait
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/waiting.cpp`, write a function called `takeIn` that takes a ticket as an `int` and an item as a reference to a `const std::string`. It makes a new `Repair` with that ticket and item with `new`, so that it lives on after the function ends, and gives back the pointer `new` gave, as a `Repair*`.

Check takes in three repairs of its own, reads each one through the pointer it got, logs minutes on one, and then deletes each repair itself. It counts, with a `Repair` of its own, how many repairs `new` made, that each is used only while it lives, and that none is left at the end.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with `Repair*` in front of the name.
Make the repair with `new`, from the ticket and the item.
Give back the pointer `new` gave you.
In `main`, take in two repairs, print their items through the pointers, then delete both.
hints: A local variable ends at the function's closing `}`, whatever pointer is kept to it. A repair that has to wait for days must live somewhere that does not end with the function.
`new` makes the repair on the heap, where it stays until a `delete` ends it, and gives back its address. Whoever holds that address is now the one who must delete it.
The shape is `return new Repair(ticket, item);`.

tasks.title: Close a repair and give back its minutes
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a function called `closeRepair` that takes a pointer to a repair made with `new`, as a `Repair*`, and gives back an `int`. It gives back the repair's minutes and deletes the repair, so nothing is left of it. When the pointer is `nullptr`, it deletes nothing and gives back `0`.

Check makes repairs of its own with `new`, logs minutes on them, and hands them to `closeRepair`, and once with `nullptr`. It counts, with a `Repair` of its own, that each repair it hands over ends exactly once, and is not used after it ended.
nextSteps: Write the first line: `int`, the name, and the pointer.
Give back `0` straight away when the pointer is `nullptr`.
Keep the repair's minutes in a variable, then delete the repair.
Give back the variable. In `main`, close a repair you took in, and watch its destructor's line.
hints: After `delete`, the repair is gone: anything read through the pointer afterwards has no promised value, even though the pointer still holds the same address.
Read what you need into a variable of your own first; the variable keeps its value after the repair ends. One `delete` per repair, never two.
The shape is `if (repair == nullptr) { return 0; } int minutes = repair->getMinutes(); delete repair; return minutes;`.

tasks.title: Take a repair off the shelf
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a function called `takeOff` that takes the shelf as a reference to a `std::vector<Repair*>`, whose pointers each point at a repair made with `new`, and a ticket as an `int`, and gives back a `bool`. It deletes the repair with that ticket, takes its pointer off the shelf, keeps the other pointers in their order, and gives back `true`. When no repair on the shelf has that ticket, it changes nothing and gives back `false`.

Check fills shelves of its own with repairs made with `new`, takes off the first, a middle and the last, a ticket that is not there, and one from an empty shelf. Then it reads every repair its shelf still points at, and deletes them. It counts, with a `Repair` of its own, which repairs ended during the call and that none is left at the end. Check builds this task with the library's guard, which stops a program that reads a vector past its end.
nextSteps: Write the first line, with the shelf taken by reference.
Walk the shelf with a counted loop, and compare each repair's ticket through its pointer.
When it matches, delete the repair, then `erase` its pointer from the shelf, and give back `true`.
After the loop, give back `false`. In `main`, take a repair off and print what the shelf still holds.
hints: The shelf holds pointers, not repairs. Taking a pointer off the shelf does not end the repair, and deleting the repair does not take its pointer off: both have to happen.
The order matters: the pointer at that position is the right one only until erase moves the others up one place, so end the repair before its place goes.
The shape is `for (std::size_t i = 0; i < shelf.size(); i++) { if (shelf[i]->getTicket() == ticket) { delete shelf[i]; shelf.erase(shelf.begin() + i); return true; } } return false;`.
